newsitem.title: USA: Rowan says cannot keep pace with demand.
newsitem.headline: Rowan says cannot keep pace with demand.

text.p: Rowan Cos Inc, reporting first quarter results up from a year ago but below Wall Street estimates, said Monday that demand for its services is far outstripping its ability to deliver.

Rowan reported first quarter operating income per share of $0.09. Analysts' consensus estimate was $0.16. The company said results were hurt by a loss of $20 million, or $0.23 per share, from turnkey operations.
Rowan said it has no turnkey wells now in operation, and has no plans for additional turnkey work.

"Our primary challenge is to equitably and profitably manage our resources -- the men, money and machines -- during the ever-changing dynamics of the new business environment," Rowan Chairman C.R. Palmer said in a statement. "Current demand is far outstripping our ability to deliver, in each of our operating divisions. We must be ever vigilant to avoid making further costly mistakes."
Rowan provides offshore contract drilling and aviation services, among other operations.
